summary: TASK-070 (REQ-104 dead-code / shell-capability deletion), independent THIRD-round review of candidate 19bba4ef, focused on the two fixes the r2 repair claims (N1 = src-tauri/src/sync/mod.rs module header, N2 = src-tauri/tests/sync_e2e.rs header/banner/names/messages) and on whether this round introduced yet another inaccuracy. I did not write any of this code. I re-bound the candidate myself (all 157 candidate_files sha256 match the worktree, 0 mismatched/missing; the 17 modified non-workflow files are all inside allowed_paths; no untracked files outside .workflow-kit), re-ran three of the four gates (cargo test exit 0 = 27 suites / 177 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored, matching the record and the baseline suite-by-suite and test-name-by-test-name; npm run lint exit 0 = 0 warnings / 0 errors; npm run test:frontend exit 0 = 26/26 + 277/277 = 303/303) and read the recorded build log (exit 0). The r2->r3 delta is genuinely comment-only: a per-hunk comparison of the two cumulative-diff artifacts and a whitespace-insensitive diff of sync_e2e.rs against HEAD show the only edits are comment text, the local name fallback->ingested, two println prefixes and two expect/assert message strings - the assertion predicates themselves are unchanged (18 assert macros on both sides; the only textual difference is the reworded message of the source='miniflux' assertion, which the artifact discloses). The cited mutation reproduces: deleting ONLY the set_feed_fetch_state(...,true,...) call leaves this suite green and the entry ingested, so the real trigger is the remote_id binding, exactly as the new note says. N1 is only partly fixed and N2 is not fixed cleanly: the r3 sync/mod.rs header now correctly states the HEAD-time facts (no failure-triggered backend pull exists; fetch_failed is serialized to the frontend badge via FeedRow -> commands/folders.rs list_feeds -> api.ts fetchFailed -> Sidebar feed-error-dot; backoff is carried by fail_count/next_retry_at in set_feed_fetch_state and filtered by feeds_due_for_refresh), but it replaces the old error with a new false historical claim ('该兜底能力从未实现' - never implemented), when the fallback demonstrably WAS implemented and production-reachable in history and was deleted by the 2026-09-07 protocol switch; and the rewritten line-77 comment in sync_e2e.rs ('源未绑定 -> 本轮不该建新条目') is contradicted by this very suite, which I instrumented to read the DB after the first sync: the unbound remote feed 11 is bound and its new entry IS created in that round. A third, lower-severity clause in the same new header block repeats the backoff misattribution N1 flagged in r1. Everything else previously verified still holds: nine deletions had zero production call sites at baseline, no new dead_code/unused warnings (identical warning multiset vs the baseline run), zero residue of fallback_entries / api.syncNow / STATE_FILE_NAME, no manifest changes, all candidate files LF, and the user's real database untouched. Verdict FAIL on comment honesty, which is this round's entire deliverable. Every experiment was restored byte-identically (sha256 re-verified) and no temporary files remain in the repo.
findings: F-r3-1 (medium, requirements + maintainability, src-tauri/src/sync/mod.rs:7) - the replacement sentence '（TASK-070：本地直连失败的源并不存在「回退后端拉取」的路径——此前模块头宣称的 Miniflux 兜底能力从未实现。' over-claims in the historical direction with the clause '从未实现' (never implemented): that fallback WAS implemented and production-reachable. At commit 9828c8f (2026-08-31) src-tauri/src/sync.rs:296 called db::feeds_fetch_failed(conn) inside pull_entries, itself called from pub async fn sync_now (sync.rs:412-424); that function was exposed as the tauri command commands::sync_now (commands.rs:570, listed in the lib.rs generate_handler) and reached from the frontend through api.syncNow() -> inv('sync_now'), which src/store.ts:691 actually called. Commit 51dc66e (2026-09-05) kept the same reachable path, with feeds_fetch_failed_bound feeding the 'for feed in &failed_feeds' loop that called upsert_miniflux_entry. The very header line under review ('③ 兜底：直连失败的源从 Miniflux 拉条目（source='miniflux'）') is literally the header at 9828c8f, i.e. it was TRUE when written; it only became stale when 0ba940f (2026-09-07, 'refactor(sync): sync.rs 协议切换 Miniflux→Google Reader') deleted the failed_feeds loop and left the column with no Rust reader. I acknowledge the one reading under which the clause could survive - 0ba940f is also the commit that introduced the Google Reader architecture this module documents, so within the GReader era the fallback indeed never existed - but the sentence as written is unqualified ('此前模块头宣称的...能力从未实现') and a reader will take it as a statement about the project's history, which git refutes. The accurate wording is 'the fallback existed until the Google Reader protocol switch (0ba940f) removed it; the header has been stale since'. This is a NEW over-claim introduced by this round: the r1 review's F1 asserted only that no such path exists TODAY (present tense, true), and the r2 repair escalated that into a historical absolute - the same class of defect that failed the previous two rounds. The remaining clauses of this header are accurate and I verified each against the code (see the requirements and maintainability checks).

F-r3-2 (medium, maintainability, src-tauri/tests/sync_e2e.rs:77) - the reworded comment '// 远端另一条目（源未绑定 → 本轮不该建新条目；状态 Pull 只做状态合并，无 URL 匹配）' is false and contradicts this suite's own assertions. I instrumented the candidate (temporarily, then restored byte-identically to sha256 9e0713e0...) to read the database immediately after the first sync: articles were exactly [(1, feed 1, 'Local Article', direct), (2, feed 2, 'Remote only article', miniflux, url=http://example.com/only-remote)] and feeds.feed_url='http://example.com/remote-only.xml' had remote_id=Some(11). So the first sync DOES create the new entry for the not-yet-bound remote feed 11 and DOES bind feed 11 - the very facts asserted two lines later at sync_e2e.rs:119-120 ('remote-only feed pulled to local' / remote_id == 11). The clause '本轮不该建新条目' is therefore untrue, and its stated reason ('无 URL 匹配') is not the operative rule: the new-entry path (src-tauri/src/sync/entries.rs:145-151) upserts precisely when the URL and remote_id lookups both miss but the entry's remote feed was bound by the same round's pull_feeds, which is why report.pulled_entries is 2 after sync 1. Note the pre-task text also said '不该建新条目', so the defect is not introduced from nothing - but the r2 artifact explicitly claims this line was corrected ('line 77's related wording corrected'), and the replacement asserts a new causal chain that the code and the test's own assertions refute, so the round did not achieve the fix it reports.

F-r3-3 (low, maintainability, src-tauri/tests/sync_e2e.rs:8-9) - the new note's closing sentence 'fetch_failed 的真实用途是前端失败标记与调度退避（按 fail_count/next_retry_at 计算）' lists scheduling backoff as a use of feeds.fetch_failed while its own parenthesis says the backoff is computed from fail_count / next_retry_at. That is the same misattribution the r2 review flagged as N1 for r1's wording ('feeds.fetch_failed 只驱动指数退避重试'): the flag does not drive backoff at all - set_feed_fetch_state writes fetch_failed, fail_count and next_retry_at in one statement (src-tauri/src/db/feeds.rs:123-138) and feeds_due_for_refresh filters solely on last_fetched_at and next_retry_at (src-tauri/src/db/feeds.rs:151-157); fetch_failed itself has no reader in Rust. The sibling header in sync/mod.rs expresses this correctly in the same round, so the two new comments in the same commit are not mutually consistent. Severity is low because the parenthesis does name the real backoff columns, but on a task whose only deliverable is comment accuracy, a self-contradicting clause is a defect.

review_checks.analysis: Item-by-item against the seven acceptance criteria, verified independently. Candidate binding: recomputed sha256 for all 157 candidate_files - 157/157 match, 0 mismatched, 0 missing. Only 17 non-.workflow-kit paths are modified and every one is inside allowed_paths; no untracked file outside .workflow-kit, so there is no scope creep by file. (1) Zero production call sites: verified with git grep against HEAD (the pre-task baseline commit 621531a), not just the worktree. feeds_fetch_failed / feeds_fetch_failed_bound / feeds_origin_remote appear at HEAD only as definitions plus the db.rs re-export; article_matches_remote_feed / article_id_by_url / article_has_pending_sync / feed_by_remote_id / set_folder_remote_id only as definitions, the re-export and test files; ingestion::refresh_feed has no caller (commands/articles.rs:209 uses refresh_feed_staged, as does scheduler.rs:147); GReaderClient::mark_all_read / subscribe have no caller (production goes through db mark_all_read and quick_add/edit_subscription); fallback_entries had no increment anywhere, only the mutually-copying assignments at phases.rs:90 and commands/sync.rs:269; api.syncNow had no caller; STATE_FILE_NAME had no reference; AiEvent::Error was constructed only by its own test. I also checked the history so that the deletion did not manufacture deadness: feeds_fetch_failed_bound did have a production call site at 51dc66e, but it was already removed by 0ba940f (2026-09-07), long before this task's baseline, so all nine deletions were genuinely dead BEFORE the change. (2) Four gates green: recorded cargo_test stdout aggregates to exactly 177 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored over 27 suites; lint stdout is 'Found 0 warnings and 0 errors' with exit 0; build stdout ends in a successful Vite build with exit 0 and an empty stderr; frontend stdout ends in 26/26, 277/277, 303/303 with exit 0. I re-ran cargo test (177/0/9, exit 0), lint (0/0, exit 0) and test:frontend (303/303, exit 0) myself; I did not re-run build, per instruction. (3) Zero residue: git grep over src, src-tauri/src, src-tauri/tests and tools for fallback_entries, fallbackEntries, syncNow and STATE_FILE_NAME returns empty (rc=1). (4) AiEvent::Error removed together with its test assertions, with the file-internal test kept for Delta/Done. (5) FAILS: sync/mod.rs no longer claims a nonexistent Miniflux fallback, but the replacement introduces a false historical claim (finding F-r3-1), so the criterion 'the module header's fallback claim is consistent with the implementation' is only half met - the present-tense half is right, the '从未实现' half is wrong. (6) No new dependencies: git diff HEAD is empty for package.json, package-lock.json, src-tauri/Cargo.toml and src-tauri/Cargo.lock; all 157 candidate files are LF (zero contain CRLF); the user's real database %APPDATA%\com.fluxreader.app\fluxreader.db is still 90112 bytes, sha256 419b118e050a08c204a50603f2d5188d8132fa94d75ea417392fe7e984293550, mtime 2026-09-19 01:58:09 - untouched. (7) Retired assertions had dead objects only; the three adapted ones were rewritten onto surviving production entry points (verified by mutation, see the regression check), and the nine-deletion inventory is reflected consistently across Rust and TypeScript. No miss or scope creep found other than the header clause above; in particular nothing was rolled back and no behaviour changed.

I read the actual gate commands and raw outputs and re-ran three gates myself. cargo_test: the recorded stdout has 27 'test result:' lines aggregating to 177 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored, and my own run reproduces 27 suites / 177 / 0 / 9 with exit 0; the per-suite pass counts are identical between my run and the recorded r3 run modulo wall-clock times, and the set of 213 executed test-case names is IDENTICAL between the r2 candidate run, the recorded r3 run and my run; against the baseline RUN-5380e8e4 the same 213 names differ by exactly one rename (article_id_by_url_uses_normalized_match -> normalized_url_match_same_article) with zero net disappearance, so coverage was not silently dropped. No new warnings: normalising the cargo_test stderr warning lines gives the same multiset for the baseline and r3 (1 lib linker warning, 3 'multiple methods are never used', 1 'set_fail_edit_tag/set_fail_item_contents/set_fail_read_list_ids are never used', plus per-target duplicates); the only difference between the two runs is which test target is credited with the duplicate, a scheduling artifact - my own run shows the same artifact in the opposite direction. lint stdout is 'Found 0 warnings and 0 errors. Finished in 24ms on 65 files with 116 rules' with exit 0 in my own run. frontend stdout ends with '既有回归 26/26 通过', '新增 store 行为断言 277/277 通过', '前端逻辑回归合计 303/303 通过' and exit 0 in my own run. build I did not re-run (per instruction), but the recorded stdout shows a completed Vite build with exit 0 and a zero-byte stderr. Do the adapted tests still have teeth? I re-verified by mutation rather than trusting the narrative: forcing sync_match_maps to write a None feed component into id_to_mf_pair makes dedup_sync_e2e::cross_feed_remote_entry_cannot_write_state_or_steal_binding FAIL at dedup_sync_e2e.rs:247, so the maps-layer trust assertion still detects the cross-source regression it was adapted to guard; the mutated file was restored byte-identically (sha256 e366ccf6...) and re-hashed. I also re-ran the mutation the new sync_e2e header cites - removing ONLY the db::set_feed_fetch_state(...,true,...) call - and confirmed the suite stays green and pulled_entries is still 3, so the header's factual core about the real trigger is correct. After restoring, sync_e2e, dedup_sync_e2e, sync_content_e2e and account_lifecycle_e2e all pass (1/3/7/6).

For a deletion task I looked specifically for paths where a deleted symbol could still be reachable at runtime, including references a plain symbol grep would miss, plus string-based and rarely-exercised paths. (a) String / IPC level: the removed frontend method api.syncNow was the only sender of the 'sync_now' invoke name; git grep shows no file anywhere still contains 'syncNow' or an inv('sync_now'), while the Rust command commands::sync_now remains registered (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:258) and functional because this round changed its body to delegate to sync::sync_now with identical semantics (feeds_phase then states_phase(full=true), same error merge), so no live IPC surface was orphaned. The full-sync UI path still goes through api.syncPhase -> inv('sync_phase'), which is untouched. (b) Serialized field names: 'fallback_entries' was removed from the Rust struct (sync/mod.rs:31-38), from the TypeScript interface (src/lib/api.ts:96-103) and from the regression harness mock, and no reader remains, so there is no 'reads undefined' path. The retained AiEvent tags 'delta' and 'done' are byte-identical and the never-emitted 'error' tag was dropped from the emitter while the receiver branch was kept, so a stray/unknown channel message still surfaces an error rather than being silently discarded. (c) Database columns read elsewhere: the deletion removed Rust query helpers, not schema - feeds.fetch_failed still exists (db/migrations.rs:33), is still written by set_feed_fetch_state (db/feeds.rs:125) and is still read: FeedRow derives Serialize and carries the field (db/feeds.rs:16), it is handed out by the list_feeds command (commands/folders.rs:103-105, registered at lib.rs:230), typed at src/lib/api.ts:57, mapped to fetchFailed at api.ts:534 and consumed by the sidebar badge at src/components/Sidebar.tsx:240-247. So the flag's remaining consumer is intact and no UI path was orphaned; migrations are untouched, so existing databases stay compatible. (d) Rarely exercised branches: both scheduler entry points still obtain ids through feeds_due_for_refresh / feeds_all_ids (scheduler.rs:115 and :123), whose SQL filters on last_fetched_at and next_retry_at and does not read fetch_failed, so removing the three fetch_failed queries changed no scheduling path. (e) Empty / repeated execution: sync_now stays idempotent (pull merge is upsert-based) and the command now shares one implementation with sync::sync_now instead of duplicating it. No runtime reachability defect found; the defects I do report are comment-accuracy ones, recorded under requirements and maintainability.

This round's entire deliverable is comment honesty, so I judged every rewritten clause strictly, in both directions, and re-checked the comments fixed in earlier rounds. Accurate and verified: the sync/mod.rs clauses that no failure-triggered backend pull exists; that origin='remote' feeds are covered implicitly by the reading-list pull (greader_pull.rs:27-80, pulled via user/-/state/com.google/reading-list) and by the Fever unread+saved reconciliation (fever_pull.rs:46-127, :157-177), so no local direct fetch is needed for them; that fetch_failed is serialized to the frontend badge (FeedRow -> commands/folders.rs:103 list_feeds -> api.ts:57/:534 fetchFailed -> Sidebar.tsx:240 feed-error-dot, confirmed end to end); and that backoff is carried by fail_count / next_retry_at (db/feeds.rs:123-138 writes them; db/feeds.rs:151-157 filters on next_retry_at, and set_feed_fetch_state is the only writer of both). Also still accurate from the earlier rounds: sync_map.rs's block header and the six SyncMatchMaps field docs no longer cross-reference deleted helpers and describe the real semantics ('None 表示未绑定', id_to_mf_pair as the same_feed_trusted input, confirmed against sync_match_maps:62-88 and sync/entries.rs:82-89/:119-128); ingestion.rs:1-7 records that the old 'Miniflux fallback query' claim was untrue and that the fallback queries were deleted as dead code; commands/ai.rs documents why the enum variant went away; commands/sync.rs explains the de-duplication motive and really does collapse two implementations into one; mock_greader.rs documents the removed unreachable ac=='subscribe' arm while subscribed_urls is still recorded by the quickadd branch and subscription_edits before the match; get_first_folder_id carries a truthful keep-and-hand-off note (its only remaining references are the db.rs re-export, an in-crate test outside allowed_paths, and comments). Why FAIL: three clauses in the newly written text are not true. (i) sync/mod.rs:7 asserts the Miniflux fallback capability was 'never implemented', which git history refutes - it existed and was production-reachable until 0ba940f (see finding F-r3-1). (ii) sync_e2e.rs:77 asserts that an unbound source must not create a new entry this round, which this suite's own assertions and my instrumented run disprove - the entry IS created and the feed IS bound in sync 1 (see finding F-r3-2). (iii) sync_e2e.rs:8-9 lists scheduling backoff as a use of fetch_failed while its parenthesis attributes the backoff to fail_count/next_retry_at, contradicting both the code and the sibling header in sync/mod.rs written in the same round (see finding F-r3-3). Everything else in the touched files that still says '兜底' has a legitimate different meaning (add_feed default-folder fallback, favicon fallback, URL-matching fallback, defensive AI-channel fallback, extract_fulltext cover fallback), and the out-of-scope stale sites (src/types.ts:44/:70, staged_refresh_e2e.rs:195, sync_phases_e2e.rs:246/:283) are correctly recorded as belonging to files outside allowed_paths - with the note that src/types.ts is not in this task's allowed_paths list while src/lib/types.ts is, so the artifact's 'outside allowed_paths' justification is right for the file it names.

Not applicable to this change, with a concrete reason rather than an invented benchmark. This is a pure deletion plus one equivalent delegation, and neither round of repair touched executable code: a per-hunk comparison of the r2 and r3 cumulative-diff artifacts shows the only differences are comment text in sync/mod.rs and sync_e2e.rs plus the narrative header of tools/frontend-regression.mjs, and the r2->r3 diff of sync_e2e.rs contains no assertion, setup call, SQL literal or expected value change. (1) Everything deleted had zero call sites, so none of it ever executed at runtime: the three Miniflux-fallback queries, the old non-staged ingestion::refresh_feed, GReaderClient::mark_all_read / subscribe, the five superseded per-item queries, STATE_FILE_NAME and api.syncNow. (2) The structure that actually determines sync cost is untouched: sync_match_maps still issues the same 5 batch queries and the merge loop still performs O(1) HashMap/HashSet lookups (db/sync_map.rs:47-122, consumed at sync/entries.rs:99-154), so query count and per-entry work are unchanged. (3) The only executed-code change in the whole task, commands::sync_now delegating to sync::sync_now, preserves the sequence feeds_phase (push_feeds + pull_feeds) then states_phase(full=true) and the same error-merge arithmetic (sync/phases.rs:82-92); the single removed operation is one O(1) copy of the deleted fallback_entries counter, nanoseconds against network I/O and SQLite work. (4) The task's quality-goal performance targets (ten-thousand-item startup, layout switching, social-layout article loading) belong to REQ-001/003 and are not on this deletion surface; no workload, baseline or measurement exists for them here, so I fabricated none and claim no speedup.
